policy: Append directly traceable exact-taxon organ evidence ONLY. No negative inference, no county nativity or voucher certification; retain original master JSON, source photos, rights and scores. Sex/stage/variant observations are conditional.

evidence.source: Flora of North America, Poa annua treatment via Burke Herbarium
evidence.note: Leaf sheaths CLOSED for approximately the basal one-third of their length; sheath may be free/open above closure. Score true fused sheath margins, not overlapping but separate edges.

evidence.source: Flora of North America, Poa annua treatment via Burke Herbarium
evidence.note: Culms described as prostrate TO erect, 2–20(–45) cm; prostrate refers to the actual flowering culm and is variable, not automatically a stolon or every individual.

evidence.source: Kew GrassBase, Eragrostis spectabilis, separate lower/upper glume descriptions
evidence.note: Lower glume: 1-veined; upper glume: 1-veined. Separate organs described in this exact species, not a lemma or spikelet rachilla vein.

evidence.source: Kew GrassBase, Melinis repens exact species under accepted name
evidence.note: LOWER STERILE floret lemma may be mucronate or bear a single awn 0–7(–10) mm long; UPPER fertile lemma is a different, short hard structure without this awn. Awn varies, and does not arise from a glume.

evidence.source: Kew GrassBase, Melinis repens exact species
evidence.note: Lower sterile lemma is glabrous OR villous, with white/purple hairs that can reach 2–6 mm; not hairs on the spikelet stalk, fertile lemma or glumes. The observation is conditional.

evidence.source: Kew GrassBase, Cortaderia selloana, female fertile florets
evidence.note: PISTILLATE/female fertile lemmas have long silky hairs 4–8 mm, especially below; male spikelets can be glabrous. Score only when floret sex is established, not on a whole-plume photo.

evidence.source: Kew GrassBase, Nassella tenuissima, floret callus
evidence.note: The floret callus is pilose, around 0.2–0.4 mm; hairs are near one-quarter to one-third fertile lemma length. Distinguish hairs at the callus from those of lemma surface, rachilla or glume.

evidence.source: Gould (1975), Grasses of Texas, Chloris canterai/canterae printed account; modern Stapfochloa canterae
evidence.note: The actual FERTILE lower floret lemma bears one 2.4–5.5 mm awn; some fall within the Lab's 2–5 mm band, others extend beyond it. The additional lowest sterile floret awn (about 1.5–3.5 mm) is a different organ. Conditional bin match only.
evidence.organ_scope: fertile floret lemma, not sterile floret
